renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: decay_curve
  title: Contact frequency against distance
  description: |-
    Each curve is a sample: the mean contact frequency between pairs of bins at each genomic distance, on log axes. It answers how quickly interactions fade with distance in the library.
    How to read: contact frequency should fall smoothly as distance grows. A plateau or a bump at long range may point to an artefact. HiCExplorer publishes no cut-off for the decay.
    Note: the first bin, at distance zero, is not shown on a log axis.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/deeptools/HiCExplorer/master/hicexplorer/hicPlotDistVsCounts.py
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Genomic distance (bp)
    y_title: Mean contact frequency
    log_x: true
    log_y: true
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: distance
    y: contacts

- component: card
  title: Contact frequency range
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest mean contact frequency of any distance bin, which is the shortest distance, with the median and the lowest bin next to it. It answers how steeply contacts fall across the distance range.
    How to read: the values span orders of magnitude, so a large gap between the maximum and the median is normal. Use the curve to compare samples rather than this number.
  column: contacts
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: shortest-distance bin, with the median and the lowest

- component: table
  title: Contact frequency per distance bin
  description: |-
    Each row is a distance bin of one sample: the mean contact frequency, the number of bins behind it and the scale factor HiCExplorer wrote. It answers the exact value behind each point of the curve.
    How to read: read the number of bins next to each value, since a bin with few bins behind it is noisier.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/deeptools/HiCExplorer/master/hicexplorer/hicPlotDistVsCounts.py
